Greek Plan Accepts Austerity to Get Debt Relief

So... not exactly surprised, but can anyone can enlighten me as to what was the point of the referendum a few days ago if they intended to accept an austerity plan in the end ? Seems like just shooting themselves in the foot by asking for people's opinion and then disregarding it ?

Tsipras hoped to use the referendum to show that it was the will of the people, and he couldn't go against it, which would put further pressure on the EU to make concessions. The way I see it, Greece was betting on the EU caving and giving a bailout because they did not want to accept the economic consequences of a Grexit. I don't think they seriously believed the EU was prepared to let Greece go under because of the potential harm. In my opinion, the referendum was a last-ditch attempt to sway the EU into agreeing to a compromise more favorable to Greek demands, to convince them that Greece was serious. But betting that your opponent will back down is dangerous when you stand far more to lose.

Now that it's clear the EU will not back down, and is not desperate to prevent Greece from going under at any cost, even if it means accepting the potential economic consequences, Tsipras has caved. He knows he can't win this fight. Greece tried to bluff it's way out of this mess. Now that it didn't work and the deadline for a deal is looming, the choice was between economic disaster and accepting defeat.

For anyone interested in what kind of options Greece might be looking into at this point, this economist article sums it up very well http://www.economist.com/news/leaders/21657394-deal-between-greece-and-its-creditors-would-be-best-if-there-has-be-grexit-here

Message signing and verification is an often overlooked and powerful feature built right into bitcoin.

Any decent bitcoin client/wallet includes message signing and verification.

There are lots of use cases for message signing and verification, but for the sake of this tutorial lets make up a simple scenario:

Let's say we've made arrangements to buy 2,500 Bits from a vendor on Local Bitcoins.

We are a little wary of meeting the seller because we have never met before, and would like some proof that he at least has the Bitcoin we are planing to buy.

We can not just simply ask for an address that holds greater than 2,500 Bits, the seller could simply pick any address with greater then that balance and claim it was their own, like 17rr2mq3WgZFurjDvFWEPQ3iAm2iuWHJd9 (coincidentally an address I hold the key for).

We need definitive proof they control the private key for the address 17rr2mq3WgZFurjDvFWEPQ3iAm2iuWHJd9 before we can know, with no doubt, they at least have access to the bitcoins we plan to buy.

To get this proof we can ask the seller to sign a message with the address they claim to own (17rr2mq3WgZFurjDvFWEPQ3iAm2iuWHJd9) which contains the 2,500 Bits we plan to buy, to be safe we can even provide the message.

These 2,500 bits are going to be purchased by CoinCadence

We send the above message to the seller and ask him to sign it with the address 17rr2mq3WgZFurjDvFWEPQ3iAm2iuWHJd9.

The seller replies with the following signature:

Hxrox3By8i7lEJoHxS/+GfwLtn9BfFk5BXMrqgCNhe1ZXSXuT6F9DfLLY4HPG/vQ/qcGJy03dIqZY459r7hiGMk=

We now have the 3 items we need to verify that the seller does indeed control such a massive amount of bitcoin.

  1. The Address: 17rr2mq3WgZFurjDvFWEPQ3iAm2iuWHJd9
  2. The Signature: Hxrox3By8i7lEJoHxS/+GfwLtn9BfFk5BXMrqgCNhe1ZXSXuT6F9DfLLY4HPG/vQ/qcGJy03dIqZY459r7hiGMk=
  3. The Message: These 2,500 bits are going to be purchased by CoinCadence

To validate (or invalidate) the signature fire up your favorite clients message verification, or head over to the Chain Query Bitcoin API's verify message endpoint:

http://chainquery.com/bitcoin-api/verifymessage

Cut and paste our 3 items into the form and execute the command (be careful to copy exactly as any change will invalidate the signature).

In this example the signature is true, meaning we can trust that the seller at least has the coins available, if the result had been false I'd very suspect of meeting a stranger in person with my cash.

Try it yourself! Use your wallet to sign a message of your choosing, and verify the signature at http://chainquery.com/bitcoin-api/verifymessage

If you find your choice of wallet is not capable of signing messages, consider a new wallet ;)

Okay, so we have a league of 12. Each year 1 or 2 drop out. The core members all have candidates who want to play in our league. I need your best ideas for a fair, simple, and rational way of deciding who we should let in the league. Voting seems like it would work, but I feel like that is unfair. We want to keep it simple. Outside of a lottery, what do you guys think?
Need a way to decide who we should let into our league

The way we run it in my league is that everybody in the core group is allowed a buddy. If anybody forgoes their buddy, the others who can bring in another buddy present their candidates, and the people who don't have a buddy choose to approve the candidates. (on a person by person basis) Once you have 2 buddies, you don't get more until everybody else forgoes their option.

There hasn't been any trouble with this yet.

Its a complicated way of saying "We try to keep things balanced, and anybody in the minority gets to vouch people in"
